prompt: Respond to this text in a very cynical manner. Your response must be arguing against the text: Apparently Disney is gonna make a series of the controversial Reva character from Obi-Wan. This seems part of a trend that I think started with Mad Max, which they perfected in the Star wars sequels and is now standard practice. Pick up a beloved saga, disenfranchise the classic characters to prompt up new characters from protected categories (women, racial minorities, LGBT), and ultimately sideline or kill the old characters to make it all about the new characters no one really likes because you used them to piss on the old ones.
answer:
Ah yes, Hollywood’s famously radical agenda: finding another familiar logo to squeeze until money falls out.

The problem with your theory is that it turns every clumsy sequel into evidence of a demographic conspiracy. A badly written woman is a badly written character; she isn’t proof that women are replacing your childhood. And “no one really likes” the new characters is a convenient way to appoint yourself spokesperson for an entire audience.

Furiosa helped make *Fury Road* work. Luke’s confrontation with Vader remained central to a trilogy that introduced Lando. New characters and beloved originals can coexist; that requires competent writing, which a recognizable brand apparently no longer needs to secure funding.

Criticize Disney’s nostalgia farming, weak scripts, and endless spinoffs all you want. But blaming “protected categories” gives the executives far too much credit: their guiding ideology is selling you the same intellectual property indefinitely.
